rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap XCVIII Divers ways of rectifying Nativities
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first numbered natal chapter introduces multiple ways to rectify an uncertain birth time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Printed XCVIII / editorial sequential XCIX; distinct from prior unnumbered introduction.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A round natal horoscope depicts an unidentified merchant born in the year 1616.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Named occupational description, not independently documented person.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The merchant's chart appears associated with a September 19 birth date.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Calendar system and zodiac positions not independently reconstructed.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The round horoscope includes a PM time with minute/second-like notation.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Exact placement and whether correction precedes/follows figure remain unresolved.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The chart refers to geographic latitude approximately 53°.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The previous oblique-ascension table includes a 53° latitude lookup.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The printed figure depicts a horoscope's ascendant and planetary positions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Full natal figure astronomy/house geometry requires independent chart parity.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly frames natal rectification as prerequisite for forecasting actions and contingencies.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical goal, not evidence forecasts are actually accurate.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He demands accurate planetary positions before using the natal chart.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Ephemeris precision premise distinct from rectification accuracy.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The astrologer first erects a chart using an estimated reported birth time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The supplied original time may be incorrect.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He next asks whether that reported time is actually the moment of birth.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The original birth-time uncertainty is explicit.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The opening warning about checking estimated birth time continues across original PDF534–535.
rows.original_source_qualifications: One continuous introductory instruction.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: deceived wholly in the Sign ascending
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly warns that an erroneous hour may produce an entirely wrong rising sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not merely several degrees of error.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: few or no degrees or latter part
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says even within a sign an error may place Ascendant near zero degrees or near the end.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Ascendant position sensitive to clock uncertainty.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims no reliable natal judgment follows if estimated birth time is wrong.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Authorial epistemic standard, not independently validated predictive property.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He applies his warning to interpretations of appearance, health/constitution, and fortune.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Traditional categories, not validated behavioral or medical inference.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes rectification procedures to ancient authorities.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Appeal to tradition rather than a controlled test.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first way Trutine or Scrutiny of Hermes
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first method discussed is the Trutine of Hermes.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate from Animodar and event/accident rectification.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: moment infant first separated mother and received breath
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He defines the desired true natal instant as when the infant separates from the mother and first breathes.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historically specific birth-event operationalization, not today's universal birth-time recording convention.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: farre more ancient then Animodar of Ptolomey
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Trutine predates the Ptolemaic Animodar procedure.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Unverified historical chronology of methods.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He ascribes the procedure to an aphorism attributed to Ptolemy.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Authorship of the Centiloquium itself is contested, which Lilly acknowledges parenthetically.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon Signe at birth ascendant Conception
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He directs setting the Moon's zodiac sign at birth as the ascendant sign at conception.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Cross-temporal sign reciprocity; no real conception record.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon Signe at conception sign opposite birth ascendant
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says the Moon's sign at conception, or its opposite, corresponds to the natal ascendant sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The opposite-sign alternative is part of the source rule and widens matches.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: very degree same Sign Moon conception degree ascendant birth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly ascribes to Hermes the stronger view that the exact degree of the conception Moon should become the natal ascendant degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Exact-degree assertion is distinct from sign-only correspondence.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: conception date by Moon and birth Ascendant
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The method requires both a proposed conception date and natal lunar/Ascendant relations.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Both birth-time and conception-time inputs can be uncertain.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says the method had practical uses and a history of use.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Personal historical assessment, not measured calibration.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: will not many examples hold firme to a degree two or three
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He explicitly reports failure to hold exactly within one, two, or three rising degrees in many examples.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Negative precision finding rather than an exact ascendant verification.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: time mistaken by houre or two
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says it sometimes helps where the given birth time was off by one or two hours.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Coarse-hour correction aim differs from minute precision.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: His primary observed use is identifying which zodiac sign rose.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Sign-class rather than minute-level event timing.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He emphasizes exact rising degrees were seldom fixed by this approach.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A direct source limitation relevant to clock-time precision claims.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He notes Junctinus offers many supporting examples.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Third-party published example count not independently audited.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says those reports aligned with charts also rectified using life accidents.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Potential circular evaluation if accident-derived charts are used as criterion.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He names Schoner, Pontanus and Sir Christopher Heydon as supporters of the method.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical reputation not evidence of independent predictive validity.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: The Correction of an estimate Scheame by Trutine of Hermes
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly opens a separately named instruction subsection on correcting an estimated natal chart.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Still within printed Chapter XCVIII.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: year day and hour birth brought unto you
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The method starts with reported birth year, day and hour.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Initial birth time is only an estimate.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He directs erecting the natal figure and checking the Sun's position for that time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Requires a historical ephemeris and local clock.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A Moon below the horizon is classified by natal houses one through six.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This determines which gestation-duration table column to use.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: take distance Moon from Angle of East
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: For Moon below the earth, measure zodiacal distance from the Ascendant/eastern angle.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Signed direction of distance must be preserved.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: For Moon above horizon, Lilly lists houses twelve through seven.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Opposite position from the below-earth branch.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon distance from cusp seventh West
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: For Moon above horizon, use its distance from the western angle/cusp seventh.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Second distinct angular reference.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: subtract Signe and degree of Angle from Moon
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He instructs subtracting angle sign/degree from Moon's sign/degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An angular subtraction, not a measured gestation date.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: add twelve whole Signs if subtraction cannot be made
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He allows adding 12 signs to the Moon's position before subtraction to handle wraparound.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Full 360-degree modular adjustment.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: enter subsequent Table Mansion of child
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Use the computed angular distance to consult a table of months/days of an infant in utero.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical claimed gestation model, not current obstetric evidence.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: A Table of the mansion of the Child in its mothers Wombe
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The printed numeric table maps lunar distance to supposed gestation length.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Assumes a relation between chart geometry and pregnancy duration, not demonstrated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One gestation-day column is for the natal Moon under the earth.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different from the Moon-above-earth column.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon above earth from seventh house
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The second column provides a different day count for the same angular distance.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Location relative to horizon changes proposed duration.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first row shows 273 days for Moon below the earth at zero distance.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Illustrative historical numeric row, not medically supported gestation norm.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first row above-earth column gives 258 days.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different from below-earth branch.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A second printed table gives cumulative day counts by month.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Requires common versus leap-year distinction.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One column accumulates calendar days in a common year.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical civil calendar handling must be checked.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A second column gives day counts for a leap year.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Gregorian/Julian calendars and 1616 leap status need independent reconciliation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: use of these Tables and the practicall part
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly outlines how the gestation and month tables are applied.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is an algorithm, not an externally observed conception date.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: consider birth yeer Common or Bissextill
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Check whether the year of birth is common or leap.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Step one, calendar dependent.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: observe day of the yeer birth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Compute the ordinal day of the year using cumulative months and birth day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Step two; separate month-day mapping.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mansion of Child subtracted from day of Birth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Subtract the table's gestation duration from birth year-day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Step three, derives presumed conception day count.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if subtraction cannot ... add whole yeer 365 or 366
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: If the subtraction would be negative, add 365/366 before subtracting.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Cross-year modular treatment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Use the result to find the corresponding month and calendar day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Step four, constructs conjectural conception date.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: consider Moon day of Conception at noone
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Examine the Moon's zodiacal position at noon on the inferred conception day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Step five, ephemeris dependence.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly gives a 13° tolerance between calculated conception Moon and estimated natal ascendant.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A broad acceptance band, not exact degree matching.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if not distant ... day found out is conception
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: If within 13°, he accepts the proposed conception day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source judgment, no independent conception certificate.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: If farther apart, he allows good planetary aspects to advance birth timing.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Post hoc latitude in adjustment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Alternatively adverse aspects may delay birth.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Widening interpretation without calibrated offset.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in our Nativity Moon 1 44 Gemini under earth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The worked merchant chart puts the Moon at approximately 1°44 Gemini beneath the horizon.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original geometry not independently recalculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Because the Moon is below the horizon, Lilly measures from the Ascendant.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Chooses corresponding gestation column.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He represents the Moon's longitude as two whole zodiac signs plus 1°44′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An original sexagesimal sign count rather than 2° of zodiac longitude.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds a full zodiac turn when the required subtraction would otherwise be negative.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Wrap-around rule applied in practice.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The original figure supplies an estimated Ascendant near sign 9, degree 6°37′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical assumed birth time rather than an externally confirmed fact.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: distance Moon and Ascendant 4 Sign 25 degree 7
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The derived angular difference is four whole signs plus approximately 25°07′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Exact source subtraction details need independent ephemeris and sign-order check.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: table nearest 4 24 under earth gives 285 days
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He finds about 285 days in the Moon-below-earth gestation table.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical gestation approximation; not a verified clinical pregnancy term.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says the merchant's gestation-duration lookup yielded approximately 285 days.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not independently documented pregnancy duration.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: birth yeer is 1616 divided by four no remainder
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He identifies 1616 as a leap year.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Julian leap-year arithmetic independently checkable.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The merchant natal example uses September 19 as birth month/day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: One authorial chart, not an identified external birth certificate.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: From his leap-year table the cumulative days through August are 244.
He counts September 19 as the 263rd day of leap year 1616.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source month/day arithmetic independently checkable.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds a full 366-day leap year for backward gestation count crossing year boundary.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The source assumes the gestation table duration.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He obtains 629 total adjusted days.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Correct whole-day addition.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He derives conception-day ordinal 344.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Simple arithmetic; not independent evidence conception happened then.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He uses prior common-year cumulative days through November 334 and adds ten days.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This moves to December 10 in the preceding year.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He proposes Sunday 10 December 1615 as the conception date.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A constructed/retrospective conjecture, not a pregnancy record.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He places the Moon at about 28°13 Sagittarius on the proposed conception day at noon.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source ephemeris assertion not independently reconstructed.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not above 8 degrees distant Ascendant Birth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says that lunar position is within about eight degrees of the birth Ascendant.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Meets the source's loose 13° acceptance threshold.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He gives the Moon's daily motion as about 15°07′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical ephemeris value unverified.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He calculates when the Moon would reach about 6° Capricorn, the inferred birth Ascendant degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Refines conception time from lunar motion, not an observed clock.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in sixth degree Capricorn Sunday night about one clock
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He conjectures the Moon attained the desired point around 1 AM Sunday night.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Ambiguous day boundary and old-style time wording; independent lunar parity required.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Whether that be not a fit time
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He presents this as a plausible time for conception, framed as a question.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Explicit uncertainty rather than a medically confirmed conception time.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: This Nativity precisely rectified by Accidents
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says his merchant nativity was in fact rectified using accidents/life events.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Retrospective author claim, not independent accuracy benchmark.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One class of accident-based rectification depends on directions of the Midheaven.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A different astrology time-adjustment method.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He also uses directions of Ascendant to respective promissors.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Multiple directions, not same as Trutine of Hermes.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports agreement across Midheaven and Ascendant directions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: No event list, selection process or prospective holdout preserved here.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Some have delivered way to find hour Conception ... no credit
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly calls an alternative formula too fine or delicate to handle fully and expressly says he does not credit it.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Major source-negative; do not promote this method as endorsed by Lilly.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: right ascension Sun for Noon conception
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The disfavored method begins with Sun right ascension at noon on the conjectured conception day.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical recipe description only, not validated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes a reference to Capricorn in the Sun-RA calculation.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original procedural meaning requires detailed table reconstruction.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: oblique ascension Moon day Birth under latitude
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The rejected formula uses oblique ascension of the natal Moon at birthplace latitude.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Requires latitude-specific tables.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: subtract Sun RA from Moon oblique RA
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He instructs subtracting solar right ascension from lunar oblique ascension.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source arithmetic, no verified conception timestamp.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He converts remaining angular distance to time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Uses 15° equator per hour.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A variant uses adding 24 hours to avoid negative clock differences.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Modulo-day accounting.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reiterates disbelief in the method before describing it.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The author's clear reservation overrides tempting rule-extraction into active prediction.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP XCIX Of the Rectification of a Nativity by Animodar
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A new numbered Chapter XCIX begins below horizontal divider on original PDF539/printed505.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Editorial sequential C (100), separate from the Hermes chapter.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Ptolomy directs last new or full Moon before birth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Animodar opening refers to choosing the preceding new or full Moon's degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This belongs to following chapter, not Hermes's procedure.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The next method begins assigning planetary dignity to the chosen degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Next batch must read until subsequent true chapter divider.
